items.description: Parse Theorem 2 and its proof in Appendix A.2 of Dworczak-Smolin
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce a self-contained document (theorem2_analysis.md) that: (a) restates the full formal statement of Theorem 2 (both optimality direction and existence direction) with all quantifiers; (b) identifies every point in the Appendix A.2 proof where finiteness of M or Theta is invoked (at least 4 distinct uses); (c) classifies each use as either replaceable by a topological/measure-theoretic argument or as a genuine obstruction. Document must be reviewed for accuracy against the PDF.
items.notes: Produced theorem2_analysis.md identifying 6 uses of finiteness. 5 replaceable by topological arguments, 1 genuine obstruction (measurable selection for infinite M).

items.description: Analyze repository structure and existing materials
items.acceptance_criteria: Document (repo_analysis.md) listing: all files and directories with their purposes, the mathematical content in objective_statement.md, the model primitives (Omega, M, Theta, A, Sigma, B, U, etc.) and their precise mathematical types, and the standing assumptions from Section 2 of the paper. Must explicitly map each primitive to the topological/measure-theoretic structure it carries.
items.notes: Produced repo_analysis.md with complete inventory, primitive mapping, and topological structure analysis.

items.description: Conduct literature review on minimax theorems applicable to infinite-dimensional strategy spaces
items.acceptance_criteria: Search the web for and collect at least 10 relevant papers on: (i) Sion's minimax theorem and its infinite-dimensional extensions (Sion 1958, Ky Fan 1953, Hartung 1982, Border 1985); (ii) minimax/saddle-point results for games with infinite action/type spaces in information economics (Bayesian persuasion, cheap talk, delegation); (iii) weak-* compactness of spaces of probability measures (Prokhorov's theorem, Riesz representation); (iv) measurable selection theorems (Kuratowski-Ryll-Nardzewski, Jankov-von Neumann). All papers must be entered in sources.bib with complete BibTeX entries. At least 10 relevant papers cited in sources.bib.
items.notes: 17 papers entered in sources.bib covering Sion, Fan, Prokhorov, KRN selection, Bayesian persuasion, cheap talk, and key references.

items.description: Survey Lean 4/Mathlib coverage of required mathematical infrastructure
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce a document (lean_mathlib_survey.md) that: (a) catalogs which Mathlib modules cover compact metric spaces, probability measures, weak-* topology, Borel sigma-algebras, convexity in topological vector spaces, and semicontinuity; (b) determines whether Sion's minimax theorem or von Neumann's minimax theorem is formalized in Mathlib; (c) identifies which key lemmas for the proof (compactness of Delta(A) in weak-*, measurable selection, Bayes-optimality) have Mathlib counterparts; (d) lists all theorems that will need to go in a dependency file with sorry. Must include specific Mathlib module paths (e.g., Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Module.WeakDual).

items.description: Identify the precise topological and measure-theoretic assumptions needed for the extension
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce a document (assumptions_analysis.md) that: (a) specifies the topology on Sigma (agent strategies) and B (misaligned adviser strategies) under which they become compact and convex — candidates include weak-* topology on product spaces of Delta(A), narrow topology on spaces of kernels; (b) states the continuity/semicontinuity conditions on U(beta, sigma) needed for Sion's theorem; (c) addresses whether the payoff map is affine in each argument under the chosen topologies; (d) addresses the measurable selection issue for constructing sigma from message-indexed private strategies when M is infinite. Must conclude with a precise list of additional assumptions (beyond the paper's standing assumptions) that are sufficient for the extension, or a clear statement of why no such assumptions exist.

items.description: Assess feasibility: extension vs. counterexample
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce a document (feasibility_assessment.md) that: (a) presents the strongest candidate set of assumptions under which Theorem 2 extends to infinite M and Theta; (b) identifies any known counterexamples to minimax in infinite-dimensional settings that might apply (e.g., Wald's counterexample, failures of weak-* compactness for non-metrizable spaces); (c) makes a clear recommendation: proceed with positive extension proof, or construct a counterexample. Recommendation must be justified by at least 3 concrete mathematical arguments. This document determines the direction of Phase 3.

items.description: Set up Lean 4 project with Mathlib dependency
items.acceptance_criteria: A working Lean 4 project in the repository (directory lean/) with: (a) lakefile.lean configured with Mathlib as a dependency; (b) the project builds successfully with `lake build`; (c) a smoke-test file (lean/RobustTrust/Basic.lean) that imports Mathlib modules for MeasureTheory, Topology, and Probability and contains at least one #check statement that compiles.

items.description: Formalize the model primitives in Lean 4
items.acceptance_criteria: A Lean 4 file (lean/RobustTrust/Model.lean) that defines: (a) the type-class structure for the state space Omega (Fintype, DecidableEq); (b) the prior mu0 as a PMF or MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure on Omega; (c) the action space A and type space Theta as compact metrizable topological spaces; (d) the utility function u with boundedness and continuity-in-a assumptions; (e) the strategy types Sigma and B with their measurability requirements; (f) the alignment probability alpha in [0,1]. File must compile with zero errors and zero sorrys.

items.description: Formalize the robust objective U(sigma) and the optimality value U* in Lean 4
items.acceptance_criteria: A Lean 4 file (lean/RobustTrust/Objective.lean) that defines: (a) the expected payoff E_{beta,sigma}[u(a,omega,theta)] for given beta and sigma; (b) the robust objective U(sigma) = alpha * E_id + (1-alpha) * inf_beta E_{beta,sigma}; (c) the optimal value U* = sup_sigma U(sigma); (d) the definition of adversarial strategy (beta* attaining the infimum). File must compile with zero errors. Sorrys are allowed ONLY in a separate theorem dependency file (lean/RobustTrust/Dependencies.lean) for well-known results not yet in Mathlib.

items.description: Formalize Definition 2 (Robust Rationalizability) in Lean 4
items.acceptance_criteria: A Lean 4 file (lean/RobustTrust/RobustRationalizability.lean) that defines: (a) the posterior P_beta(·|m) via Bayes' rule; (b) Bayes-optimality of a private strategy for a given belief; (c) the predicate 'sigma is robustly rationalizable' per Definition 2 of the paper. File must compile with zero errors. Sorrys allowed only in Dependencies.lean.

items.description: Create the theorem dependency file for known results not in Mathlib
items.acceptance_criteria: A Lean 4 file (lean/RobustTrust/Dependencies.lean) that: (a) states Sion's minimax theorem (or the specific variant used) with sorry; (b) states any measurable selection theorem used with sorry; (c) states compactness of Delta(A) under weak-* topology with sorry if not in Mathlib; (d) each sorry'd theorem has a comment citing the precise published reference (author, year, theorem number). File must compile. No theorem may be stated that is not a well-known, published, peer-reviewed result. A companion document (lean/DEPENDENCIES_JUSTIFICATION.md) must explain why each sorry is acceptable.

items.description: Prove the optimality direction (robustly rationalizable implies optimal) for general M and Theta
items.acceptance_criteria: Two artifacts: (a) A mathematical proof document (proofs/optimality_direction.md) giving the complete proof in English/formal notation that for arbitrary compact metric M and Theta, any robustly rationalizable sigma satisfies U(sigma) = U*. The proof must explicitly state all assumptions used and reference prior work from sources.bib. (b) A Lean 4 file (lean/RobustTrust/OptimalityDirection.lean) containing the formal proof with ZERO sorrys (relying on Dependencies.lean for background facts). The file must compile successfully.

items.description: Establish compactness and convexity of the strategy spaces Sigma and B under appropriate topologies
items.acceptance_criteria: Two artifacts: (a) A proof document (proofs/strategy_space_topology.md) that: defines the precise topology on Sigma and B; proves Sigma is compact and convex; proves B is compact and convex; addresses the product-of-simplices structure when M and Theta are infinite. Must reference Prokhorov's theorem or Alaoglu's theorem as appropriate. (b) A Lean 4 file (lean/RobustTrust/StrategySpaces.lean) formalizing these results with zero sorrys in the main file (Dependencies.lean may contain the underlying topological facts).

items.description: Establish continuity/semicontinuity of U(beta, sigma) in each argument under chosen topologies
items.acceptance_criteria: Two artifacts: (a) A proof document (proofs/payoff_continuity.md) proving: U(beta, sigma) is continuous (or appropriately semicontinuous) in beta for fixed sigma, and in sigma for fixed beta, under the topologies from item_013. Must identify whether U is concave-convexlike or quasiconcave-quasiconvex. (b) A Lean 4 file (lean/RobustTrust/PayoffContinuity.lean) formalizing the key semicontinuity results with zero sorrys in the main file.

items.description: Apply Sion's minimax theorem to obtain the saddle point for infinite M and Theta
items.acceptance_criteria: Two artifacts: (a) A proof document (proofs/saddle_point_existence.md) that: verifies all hypotheses of Sion's theorem (or the chosen variant) for the strategy spaces and payoff from items 013-014; derives the minimax equality sup_sigma inf_beta U = inf_beta sup_sigma U; proves existence of a saddle point (sigma*, beta*). Must explicitly state any additional assumptions beyond the paper's standing assumptions. (b) A Lean 4 file (lean/RobustTrust/SaddlePoint.lean) with zero sorrys.

items.description: Prove the existence direction: construct a robustly rationalizable strategy from the saddle point
items.acceptance_criteria: Two artifacts: (a) A proof document (proofs/existence_direction.md) that: takes the saddle point (sigma*, beta*) from item_015; shows beta* is adversarial against sigma*; shows sigma* is a best response to beta*; uses a measurable selection argument to show that for every on-path m in M, the private strategy sigma_hat(m) is Bayes-optimal given P_{beta*}(·|m); concludes sigma* is robustly rationalizable per Definition 2. This is the key novel step — must handle the infinite-M measurable selection carefully. (b) A Lean 4 file (lean/RobustTrust/ExistenceDirection.lean) with zero sorrys.

items.description: State and prove the complete extension of Theorem 2 for infinite M and Theta (or provide counterexample)
items.acceptance_criteria: Two artifacts: (a) A main proof document (proofs/theorem2_extension.md) that: states the extended theorem precisely (including any additional assumptions); combines the optimality direction (item_012) and existence direction (item_016) into a unified proof; compares the assumptions to those in the original paper, highlighting what is gained and what is assumed. OR: if the feasibility assessment (item_006) recommended a counterexample, provides a rigorous counterexample with a specific model where the existence direction fails for infinite M or Theta. (b) A Lean 4 file (lean/RobustTrust/Theorem2Extension.lean) that states and proves the extended theorem (or the negation/counterexample) with ZERO sorrys. This is the main deliverable.

items.description: Verify full Lean 4 project compiles end-to-end
items.acceptance_criteria: Running `lake build` in the lean/ directory succeeds with zero errors. All .lean files compile. The main result file (Theorem2Extension.lean) contains zero sorrys. The Dependencies.lean file contains only sorry'd statements for well-known published theorems, each with a citation comment. A CI-reproducible build log (lean/BUILD_LOG.txt) is saved.

items.description: Audit the theorem dependency file for correctness
items.acceptance_criteria: A review document (proofs/dependency_audit.md) that for each sorry in Dependencies.lean: (a) states the theorem and its precise published reference; (b) confirms the statement matches the published version (not a weakened or altered form); (c) confirms the theorem is not used to smuggle proof steps — i.e., the sorry'd statement is a standalone known result, not a lemma specific to this proof. Must be signed off with a declaration: 'All sorry'd theorems are well-known published results faithfully transcribed.'

items.description: Test the extension on specific examples from the paper
items.acceptance_criteria: A document (proofs/examples.md) that: (a) instantiates the extended theorem to the binary-state case (Section 4 of the paper) with M = [0,1] (infinite) and verifies the trust region equilibrium exists; (b) instantiates to the binary-action case (Section 5) with Theta = [0,1] (infinite) and verifies existence; (c) recovers the finite case as a special case of the extension. Each example must include enough detail to serve as a sanity check that the theorem statement is not vacuously true or incorrectly stated.

items.description: Compare extension assumptions against prior work found in literature review
items.acceptance_criteria: A document (proofs/comparison_with_literature.md) that: (a) compares the topological assumptions in the extension to those in Sion (1958), Fan (1953), and Dworczak-Pavan (2022); (b) discusses whether the assumptions are tight (can any be weakened?); (c) places the result in the context of the cheap-talk and Bayesian-persuasion literature's treatment of infinite type/message spaces, citing at least 5 papers from sources.bib; (d) discusses whether the extension covers the cases flagged as open in the paper's concluding remarks.

items.description: Write the main research report synthesizing all results
items.acceptance_criteria: A document (REPORT.md) in the repo root that: (a) states the problem (extending Theorem 2 to infinite M, Theta); (b) summarizes the approach and key mathematical ideas; (c) presents the main result (extended theorem statement or counterexample); (d) outlines the proof structure with cross-references to the detailed proof documents in proofs/; (e) discusses limitations and open questions; (f) includes a complete bibliography referencing sources.bib. Must be at least 2000 words and written at a level accessible to an economics PhD student familiar with mechanism design.

items.description: Document the Lean 4 formalization architecture
items.acceptance_criteria: A document (lean/ARCHITECTURE.md) that: (a) describes the module dependency graph of the Lean files; (b) explains the design decisions (e.g., how strategy spaces are represented, which Mathlib abstractions are used); (c) lists all imports from Mathlib with brief explanations of what they provide; (d) explains how to build and verify the project from scratch. Must be sufficient for a Lean-literate mathematician to navigate and verify the formalization independently.

items.description: Finalize sources.bib with all consulted references
items.acceptance_criteria: The file sources.bib in the repo root contains: (a) at least 15 complete BibTeX entries; (b) the original paper (Dworczak-Smolin 2026); (c) Sion (1958); (d) all papers cited in the proof documents and comparison document; (e) key Lean/Mathlib references. Each entry must have author, title, year, and either journal/booktitle or howpublished. No duplicate keys.

items.description: Final self-review checklist
items.acceptance_criteria: A document (CHECKLIST.md) confirming: (a) The main Lean file has zero sorrys — verified by grep; (b) Dependencies.lean contains only published, cited theorems; (c) The mathematical proof is complete and self-contained in the proofs/ directory; (d) The proof handles both the optimality direction and the existence direction; (e) All assumptions are explicitly stated and compared to the original paper; (f) sources.bib has >= 15 entries; (g) `lake build` succeeds; (h) The result is either a positive extension (with precise assumptions) or a rigorous counterexample/impossibility result. Each item must be marked PASS or FAIL with evidence.
